Find BLS Series by Search String

Source: R/find_bls.R
find_bls.Rd

Searches a catalog of every series published by the Bureau of Labor Statistics (8.3 million series from 33 BLS programs) for titles and surveys matching a search string. The catalog is built weekly from the BLS flat files by bls-index. Use the series IDs with get_bls().

Usage

find_bls(
  search_string,
  survey = NULL,
  seasonality = NULL,
  limit = 1000,
  titles_only = FALSE,
  refresh = FALSE
)

Arguments

search_string

Character string of words to search for.

survey

Character vector of BLS program codes to search within, such as "ln" (Current Population Survey) or c("la", "ln"), ignoring case. The default, NULL, searches all programs. An unknown code is an error that lists the valid codes.

seasonality

Character vector of seasonal adjustment values to keep: one or more of "SA", "NSA" and "unknown", ignoring case. The default, NULL, keeps all.

limit

Maximum number of rows to return (default: 1000). Use Inf for all matches. When rows are cut, a message gives the total and the matches per survey.

titles_only

Logical. If TRUE, every word must match the series title; survey names and aliases are ignored. Useful with survey, as in find_bls("all items", survey = "cu", titles_only = TRUE).

refresh

Logical. If TRUE, check for a newer catalog now.

Value

A tibble with columns series_id, series_title, program (the BLS program code), survey_name, seasonal ("SA", "NSA" or "unknown"), begin_year, end_year and end_period.

Searching

Every word in search_string must match, ignoring case, in the series title, the survey name or a survey alias (such as "CPI" or "JOLTS"). Words match by the part they share with their English stem, so "nurses" also finds "nursing" and "industries" also finds "industry". When that part is shorter than four letters, the word must match a whole word, so "CES" does not match "services". A short word ending in "y" or "ies" also matches its other form, so "city" finds "cities".

Results are sorted by the number of words that match the title or a survey alias, then by title length (shortest first), then by title and series ID. Short titles tend to be the general series. Narrow a search with more words or survey.

The catalog

The first search downloads the catalog (about 33 MB) into tools::R_user_dir("epidatatools", "cache") and verifies its checksum. Later searches use that copy, and check for a newer catalog at most once every 7 days. If the check fails, for example offline, the cached catalog is used. A catalog built more than 10 days ago is reported as possibly out of date.

Settings, for testing or mirrors:

  • options(bls_index.manifest_url = ...), or else the BLS_INDEX_MANIFEST_URL environment variable: the catalog manifest to read

  • options(bls_index.cache_dir = ...): where to keep the catalog

Searching needs the arrow package, which find_bls() offers to install.

Examples

find_bls("unemployment rate", survey = "ln", seasonality = "SA")
#> # A tibble: 184 × 8
#>    series_id    series_title    program survey_name seasonal begin_year end_year
#>    <chr>        <chr>           <chr>   <chr>       <chr>         <int>    <int>
#>  1 LNS14000000  (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             1948     2026
#>  2 LNS14000000Q (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             1948     2026
#>  3 LNS14000001  (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             1948     2026
#>  4 LNS14000001Q (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             1948     2026
#>  5 LNS14032183  (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             2003     2026
#>  6 LNS14032183Q (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             2010     2026
#>  7 LNS14000003  (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             1954     2026
#>  8 LNS14000003Q (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             1954     2026
#>  9 LNS14000002  (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             1948     2026
#> 10 LNS14000002Q (Seas) Unemplo… ln      Labor Forc… SA             1948     2026
#> # ℹ 174 more rows
#> # ℹ 1 more variable: end_period <chr>

find_bls("registered nurses wages")
